function.name: calculate_investment_value
function.description: Calculate the future value of an investment given the principal, interest rate and term. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

principal.description: The initial amount of the investment. This is a float type value.

interest_rate.description: The annual interest rate in percentage. Enter as a decimal (for 5%, enter 0.05). This is a float type value.

term.description: The term of the investment in years.

compounding.description: The number of times that interest is compounded per year. Default is 1 (annually).

message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Director | Why it’s worth watching |
|------|-------|----------|------------------------|
| 1978 | **The Shining** | Stanley Kubrick | Masterful atmosphere, iconic performances, psychological terror. |
| 1980 | **The Thing** | John Carpenter | Tense paranoia, groundbreaking practical effects. |
| 1984 | **A Nightmare on Elm Street** | Wes Craven | Introduced Freddy Krueger, blends dream logic with slasher thrills. |
| 1991 | **The Silence of the Lambs** | Jonathan Demme | Psychological thriller with chilling performances by Anthony Hopkins and Jodie Foster. |
| 1999 | **The Sixth Sense** | M. Night Shyamalan | Twist ending, haunting atmosphere, strong character work. |
| 2002 | **28 Days Later** | Danny Boyle | Fast‑paced zombie outbreak, gritty realism. |
| 2004 | **Saw** | James Wan | Dark, inventive horror with moral dilemmas. |
| 2007 | **Paranormal Activity** | Oren Peli | Found‑footage style, subtle dread, low budget but high impact. |
| 2010 | **The Conjuring** | James Wan | Supernatural scares, strong storytelling, sets up a franchise. |
| 2012 | **The Cabin in the Woods** | Drew Goddard | Meta‑horror that subverts tropes while delivering solid scares. |
| 2014 | **It Follows** | David Robert Mitchell | Unique premise, creepy soundtrack, effective tension. |
| 2015 | **The Witch** | Robert Eggers | Slow‑burn dread, period authenticity, unsettling atmosphere. |
| 2017 | **Get Out** | Jordan Peele | Social commentary meets horror, smart pacing, strong performances. |
| 2018 | **A Quiet Place** | John Krasinski | Silence as a weapon, emotional stakes, tense suspense. |
| 2019 | **Midsommar** | Ari Aster | Daylight horror, unsettling folk rituals, psychological depth. |
| 2020 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Modern retelling, claustrophobic tension, strong female lead. |
| 2021 | **Candyman** | Nia DaCosta | Reimagined myth, social relevance, atmospheric dread. |
| 2022 | **Evil Dead Rise** | Lee Cronin | New chapter in the franchise, visceral gore, creative set pieces. |
| 2023 | **M3GAN** | Gerard Johnstone | AI horror with a twist, commentary on tech culture, creepy doll. |

Feel free to pick based on your mood—whether you want psychological dread, supernatural chills, or a fresh take on the genre!
